reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses phase stability, microstructural inhomogeneities, and short-range order in HEAs, but provides no data or validation of the proposed integrated in-situ XRD-calorimetry technique, its synchronization, or its quantitative accuracy for fusion properties. The key premises rely entirely on uncited assumptions about experimental capabilities.
premises: High-speed synchrotron XRD can capture real-time structural disordering during HEA melting
Rapid scanning calorimetry can simultaneously measure heat flow with sub-second resolution
Correlating XRD and calorimetry signals enables direct extraction of Tm, enthalpy, entropy, and volume change
The approach yields fusion properties within 5% error relative to standard DSC and dilatometry
The method is applicable to HEAs with moderate melting points and stable liquid phases
